root_causes.description: product-catalog, a leaf service depended on by frontend/checkout/recommendation, exhibits a severe server-side p99 latency spike (~10s) while its CPU and memory usage remain flat. This injected latency propagates upstream, producing the ~9.5s p99 observed on frontend.

evidence.observed_value: p99 max=10000.0 ms, p95=8003.5 ms, mean=2010.4 ms (anomaly detected)
evidence.expected_baseline: p50≈16.1 ms; normal p99 well under 100 ms

evidence.observed_value: p99 max=9956.25 ms, p95=7971.95 ms (anomaly detected)
memory mean=23,755,980 B, max=24,018,944 B (no anomaly)

root_causes.description: frontend shows the same magnitude of p99 latency (~9.5s) because it synchronously calls product-catalog (plus recommendation → product-catalog) on the request path; its latency is inherited downstream, not intrinsic.

evidence.observed_value: p99 max=9956.25 ms, mean=2014.6 ms (anomaly detected)

root_causes.description: checkout is a downstream consumer of product-catalog but its server p99 remained normal (~24.8 ms), indicating the fault did not manifest through the checkout path during this window; low-confidence alternate.

remediation_steps: Inspect product-catalog for injected latency (chaos/flagd latency fault) and confirm whether a fixed artificial delay was introduced on its server handler or outbound calls.
Disable/revert the latency injection on product-catalog (e.g., flagd flag or chaos experiment) and re-measure p99.
Add/verify timeouts and retries between frontend→product-catalog and recommendation→product-catalog so a slow leaf cannot cascade a ~10s p99 into frontend.
Monitor product-catalog p99 (duration_milliseconds_bucket) for recovery; validate frontend p99 returns to <100 ms baseline.
Since CPU/memory are flat, avoid scaling actions — this is latency, not resource exhaustion.
